summary: A flexible row for a piece of content with optional media, title, description and actions, usable alone, as a link, or in a list (a family of Web Components).

variant.note: primary: no surface. tertiary: bordered. muted: tinted surface (muted at half strength).

size.note: medium: 16px padding and gap. small: 12px block padding, 10px gap.

href.note: Renders the whole row as a native link. Without it, or when empty, the row is a plain container. javascript:, vbscript: and data: URLs are dropped: the link renders without href and a console warning names it (SB-0115).

anatomy.name: item
anatomy.notes: A div, or an a when href is set; wraps the slotted parts, carries border, padding and the focus ring.

default.notes: sb-item-media, sb-item-content, sb-item-actions, sb-item-header and sb-item-footer.

hover.trigger: pointer over an item that has href

focus-visible.trigger: keyboard focus on an item with href
focus-visible.note: Border and a solid ring in the ring color.

accessibility.role: none for a standalone item; listitem when its parent is sb-item-group; link when href is set (native a)
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The row's text content, for an item with href (the link's name is everything inside it).
aria: sb-item-group host: role=list; sb-item inside it: role=listitem, both set when the element connects; an item moved in or out of a group gains or loses the listitem role it was given (an author role is never touched)
sb-item-separator: role=presentation, so a list has only listitem children
href: the whole row is one native link, so nested interactive controls should not be placed inside it
data-has-description and data-fixed are presentation-only attributes set by sb-item
accessibility.focusRingVisible: :focus-visible only; border and solid ring in item.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.targetSize: A linked item is at least as tall as its padding plus text (more than 24px).

openQuestions.question: How does a row become a link without a render-as-child mechanism?
openQuestions.recommendation: An href prop renders the wrapper as a native a.

openQuestions.question: List semantics: who is the list and who are the items?
openQuestions.recommendation: sb-item-group is role=list; a sb-item whose parent is the group becomes role=listitem; the separator is presentational.
openQuestions.answer: As recommended; checked in the accessibility tree.

openQuestions.question: Two-line description clamp?
openQuestions.recommendation: Drop it: clipped text hides content (WCAG 1.4.10).

openQuestions.question: Sibling rule: a second content block does not grow.
openQuestions.recommendation: sb-item marks it with data-fixed from slotchange.

elements.summary: A vertical stack of items, exposed as a list.
A thin rule between items in a group. Decorative.
elements.notes: Host role=presentation, so the list's only semantic children are its items.

elements.summary: Leading visual: an icon in a bordered tile, an image, or anything else.

variant.note: primary: no frame. icon: 32px muted tile with a border and a 16px svg. image: 40px rounded crop.

default.notes: An svg, an img or an avatar.

elements.summary: The text block: title and description.
elements.notes: Grows to fill the row. A second sb-item-content next to it does not grow (data-fixed set by sb-item).

elements.summary: The item's main text, in medium weight; can hold a badge next to the text.
Supporting text in muted color. Direct child links are underlined.
Controls at the end of the row.
A full-width row above the content.
A full-width row below the content.

useCases.when: A list of entries with an icon, a title, some text and an action
useCases.use: sb-item-group of sb-item with media, content and actions

antiPatterns.pattern: Buttons or links inside an item that has href
antiPatterns.why: Nested interactive content inside a link is invalid and confusing
antiPatterns.alternative: Drop href and put the controls in sb-item-actions

antiPatterns.pattern: A data grid made of items
antiPatterns.why: Rows and columns need table semantics

options.name: Avatar
options.reason: The code puts any element in the media slot; the activity rows in the stories use an Avatar.

options.name: Icon
options.reason: The icon media is one choice for the media slot, so the design file can turn it off for the avatar.
